It was valued at $1.4B in its September 2025 Series E, has raised about $194M, and had ARR in the “multiple $10s of millions” in 2025, with a goal of $100M by the end of 2026. Hiberly Ltd, registered in England in July 2019, lists both co-founders as its directors and as people with significant control ( Companies House ). Who owns PostHog? PostHog is private and venture-backed. Its co-founders, James Hawkins and Tim Glaser, split the company 50:50 when they started ( PostHog ); after six funding rounds, their stakes today aren’t public. Its investors include Stripe, which led the Series D ( PostHog ), Peak XV Partners, which led the Series E ( PostHog ), GV and Y Combinator. Staff own part of it too. Early employees sold shares alongside the Series C, and with the Series D “any employee could sell up to 20% of their vested shares” ( PostHog ). What is PostHog’s revenue? PostHog doesn’t publish its revenue as a number. In June 2025 co-founder James Hawkins said it had “multiple $10s of millions of ARR and 3x year-over-year growth” ( Crunchbase News ), and its goal is “$100 million in annual revenue by the end of 2026” ( PostHog handbook ). In October 2024 its handbook put revenue “in the low $10s of millions of ARR” ( PostHog handbook ). Revenue grew nearly 6x in 2022 ( PostHog ) and about 4x in 2023 ( PostHog handbook ). Stripe, which handles payments for 99% of PostHog’s paying customers, calls it “on pace for $100 million ARR” in a 2026 case study ( Stripe ). On October 16, 2026, a PostHog post still called $100M ARR, “The Hundy”, a target ( PostHog ). PostHog says it runs “default alive” and has “never had layoffs” ( PostHog ). It ended 2024 cash-flow positive ( PostHog handbook ), and in June 2025 Crunchbase News reported it was cash-flow positive but not yet profitable ( Crunchbase News ). Most users pay nothing: more than 90% of companies use PostHog for free ( PostHog ). Every product has a monthly free tier, such as 1 million analytics events and 5,000 session recordings, and usage above it is billed per unit, with no seat fees ( PostHog ). PostHog ARR (annual recurring revenue) PostHog has never published an exact ARR. Its own figures are ranges: “low $10s of millions” in October 2024 ( PostHog handbook ) and “multiple $10s of millions” in June 2025, growing 3x a year ( Crunchbase News ). Its target is $100 million ARR by the end of 2026 ( PostHog handbook ). Research firm Sacra estimated $57.5 million in February 2026 ( Sacra ); that is an outside estimate, not a PostHog figure. PostHog MRR (monthly recurring revenue) PostHog doesn’t publish MRR. “Multiple $10s of millions” of ARR means at least about $1.7 million a month, and its $100 million goal would be about $8.3 million a month; both are our calculations, not company figures. How much has PostHog raised? Funding and valuation About $194 million in six rounds, by PostHog’s count after the Series E ( PostHog handbook ); its press kit adds the rounds up to $182 million ( PostHog ). The latest is a $75 million Series E at a $1.4 billion valuation, led by Peak XV Partners in September 2025, which made it a unicorn ( PostHog ) ( Inc42 ). It has announced no round since. PostHog’s own pages date several rounds differently (its press kit puts the Series D in March 2025, for example); the table uses the announcement dates ( PostHog ). What does PostHog make? Products PostHog started in 2020 as open-source product analytics. It now sells about a dozen tools on one platform: product and web analytics, session replay, feature flags, experiments, surveys, error tracking, logs, a data warehouse, workflows and AI observability, plus PostHog AI, an assistant that answers questions about your data ( PostHog ). Since July 2026 it has positioned itself as “self-driving” software, used through its web app, Slack, an MCP server, a command-line tool and a desktop app ( PostHog ). Its code is public: the main repository is MIT-licensed outside its enterprise folder and has about 40,700 GitHub stars ( GitHub ). PostHog stopped supporting paid self-hosting in 2023 ( PostHog ); customers use PostHog Cloud in the US or the EU, hosted in Frankfurt ( PostHog ). PostHog competes on price and breadth: one platform, usage-based pricing and a free tier for every product. It publishes its own comparisons with Amplitude , Mixpanel , Heap , LaunchDarkly , Statsig , FullStory . Who is the CEO of PostHog? PostHog has two co-CEOs, its co-founders James Hawkins and Tim Glaser. They started as CEO and CTO and switched to shared titles in March 2025 ( GitHub ). Since May 2026 Hawkins has focused on AI, while Glaser runs hiring, operations, finance, go-to-market and engineering ( PostHog ). The two met at Arachnys, a London software company, where Hawkins ran sales. Where is PostHog based? Nowhere in particular: PostHog’s team is “100% remote, and distributed across more than 20 countries” ( PostHog handbook ). Its public team page lists 246 people in 33 countries on November 5, 2026 ( PostHog ), most of them in the US, the UK and Canada (our count). PostHog Inc. gives its address as 2261 Market Street #4008, San Francisco ( PostHog ). It also runs Hogpatch, an invite-only San Francisco co-working space for founders in Y Combinator’s current batch ( PostHog handbook ). What is PostHog’s email format? PostHog staff use {first}@posthog.com , 98% of known addresses per LeadIQ; people who share a first name with a colleague add a dot and their last initial.
